The packet reports an approximate signed-product representation of the unnormalized state surviving K explicitly scheduled control segments, without forming a 2^n state vector. An elementary tier has rank polynomial in 1/epsilon. A stronger interpolation tier claims polylogarithmic accuracy dependence but is not separately coded or interval-certified. The statement is conditional on the marked-CDF primitive in N663.

An application considers a sparse Poisson detector that clicks only at listed configurations while the hidden product chain continues evolving. For a finite explicit menu, it acquires both unnormalized posterior branches as signed-product mixtures and selects a myopically optimal experiment for a specified terminal-bit loss. The per-choice regret claim and costs include the observed-history probability w through log(1/w), which the source says can be acquired by precision doubling and replay. This is not a general multistep planning algorithm or a certified large-n implementation.

source_excerpts.text:
PIECEWISE-CONTROLLED PRODUCT-CHAIN SURVIVING-STATE COMPILER
2026-10-10. Constructive mathematical candidate, with a small numerical check.
No priority or independent-validation claim. No repository files changed.

Interface and inherited primitive
---------------------------------
There are n binary coordinates. On segment k of duration T_k>=0, coordinate i
has rational stationary probability p_{ki} in (0,1) and rational relaxation
rate lambda_{ki}>0. The control schedule is explicitly supplied and depends
only on the segment index and survival, not on an unobserved path. A fixed
list B={b_1,...,b_m} of distinct n-bit targets is explicit. Allow B_k to
vary by segment at no mathematical cost, provided each list is explicit.
Initially the law is a rational product Bernoulli law. All times, parameters,
and requested accuracy 0<epsilon<=1/4 have binary-rational encodings.

The one inherited computational lemma is MARKED_EVENTS.txt in the adjacent
work/target_set_resolvent directory: for any rational product starting law,
target b, rational t>=0 and alpha>0, it claims a rational alpha-accurate
marked first-hit sub-CDF F_b(t), in deterministic time polynomial in input
bits, m, and log(1/alpha). Its derivation charges target-set resolvent
conditioning, rare hits, and all precision. The theorem below is conditional
on the correctness of that internal primitive. For signed product mixtures,
call it separately on each product component and sum with signed weights.

Statement
---------
There is a deterministic algorithm which returns rational coefficients c_r
and rational Bernoulli parameters q_{ri} defining a signed product mixture

    tilde_nu_K(x)=sum_{r=1}^R c_r prod_i q_{ri}^{x_i}(1-q_{ri})^{1-x_i}

such that ||tilde_nu_K - nu_K||_1 <= epsilon, where nu_K is the exact
UNNORMALIZED law of the configuration still alive after all K control
segments. The algorithm never forms a 2^n-state vector. Its bit operation
count, output bit length, R, and sum_r |c_r| are polynomial in the explicit
input length, K, n, m, and 1/epsilon. More specifically, the elementary
geometric-age construction has

    R <= 1 + sum_k m(G_k+O(1)),
    G_k = O((nK/epsilon) log(1+T_k Lambda_k K/epsilon)
                        + (nK/epsilon) log(1+Lambda_k/gamma_k)),
    sum_r |c_r| <= 1+2K,

with gamma_k=min_i lambda_{ki}, Lambda_k=sum_i lambda_{ki}. The logarithms
are shorthand for rational bi

source_excerpts.text:
ADAPTIVE SPARSE POISSON-SENSOR POSTERIOR OPERATION
2026-10-10. Constructive internal candidate; no priority claim or publication.

The operation
-------------
An n-bit hidden configuration X evolves as independent, controlled two-state
continuous-time Markov coordinates. During one experiment, a detector clicks
at rate v_b>0 only while X=b for one of m EXPLICIT listed configurations
B={b_1,...,b_m}. It disables after its first click. The click does not
change X, which continues to evolve freely to the experiment's terminal
time T. The scientist observes only CLICK or NO CLICK, and may choose the
next detector and coordinate rates from a finite explicit menu after each
observation. All rates, times, initial product Bernoulli parameters, and
menu entries are binary rationals. The latent posterior has 2^n entries.

For each candidate experiment, the algorithm acquires signed rational
product mixtures for BOTH unnormalized posterior branches, and from them
chooses an experiment maximizing the expected accuracy of predicting a
specified terminal hidden bit. The per-choice regret can be made at most
epsilon, conditional on the observed history, in time polynomial in
input bits, n, m, menu size, history length K, log(1/epsilon), and
log(1/w), where w>0 is the probability of that history. The latter is
an explicit rare-evidence cost; it can be ACQUIRED by precision doubling
and replay of the actual history, not supplied as an ideal posterior or
oracle. The algorithm forms no 2^n-state object and has no 1/w loop.

The operation is myopic Bayes experiment selection for a concrete loss;
it does not solve arbitrary multistep planning. Its novelty relative to
ordinary conjugacy or particle filtering is the aggregate first-click
boundary measure: detector likelihoods are not assumed to preserve a
product family, and the correction generated by ALL old signed product
components is compressed into one age interpolation per detector state.
Rank grows additively along an adaptive observation path. A general
prior-art novelty comparison remains open.

Algebra of the two observation branches
---------------------------------------
For one segment let Q be the unrestricted product generator, P_t=e^{tQ},
V=diag(v_x), where v_x=v_b for x=b in B and zero otherwise, and
M_t=e^{t(Q-V)}. For any signed initial row measure zeta,

    zeta^0_T = zeta M_T,
    zeta^1_T = zeta P_T-zeta M_

MARKED FIRST-HIT EVENTS AND FINITE-BIN FEEDBACK SIMULATION
2026-10-10. Internal construction; no priority or independent-validation claim.
Companion to RESULT.txt. The same supplied product-chain interface and all its bit-cost conventions apply here.

Claim
-----
Let n independent two-state CTMC coordinates have binary-rational p_i in (0,1) and relaxation rates lambda_i>0. Let B={b_1,...,b_m} be distinct explicit configurations, and let the initial law mu be product Bernoulli with binary-rational parameters. For j in [m] define

  F_j(t)=Pr_mu(H_B<=t, X_{H_B}=b_j),
  p_j=Pr_mu(X_{H_B}=b_j)=F_j(infinity).

Given a binary-rational t>=0 and alpha in (0,1/2), each F_j(t) and p_j can be returned as rationals with absolute error at most alpha in deterministic time polynomial in input bits, m, and log(1/alpha). No 2^n-state object is formed. Consequently, for any explicit finite list of binary-rational time-bin endpoints, a rational joint law of (first-hit label, time bin) can be produced within total variation eta in time polynomial in the input, m, bin count, and log(1/eta). The distribution can be sampled exactly from fair bits at expected polynomial cost.

For a K-event feedback experiment, suppose the policy sees only previous first-hit labels and time bins. At each event it chooses new binary-rational coordinate parameters and either starts from the just-hit configuration or supplies a new binary-rational product reset law. Assume this policy is computable in polynomial time and that all generated parameter bit lengths, target-list lengths, bin counts, and transcript encodings remain polynomially bounded in the stated input and K. Approximating each conditional marked-event kernel within eta/K total variation gives a simulator whose complete length-K observed transcript law is within eta total variation of the true policy experiment. Runtime is polynomial in K, n, m, the policy/input bit lengths, maximum bin count, and log(K/eta). The physical waiting times may be exponentially large; runtime has no factor proportional to them or to 1/pi(B).

This theorem concerns the discrete observations of labels and supplied bins. It does not supply exact continuous hit times or a total-variation approximation to their continuous law. A policy inspecting time more finely than the supplied bins, hidden pre-hit trajectories, or a nonproduct posterior/reset law falls outside
